329080.definition_and_quantifier_recovery: Chord diagram = based double-occurrence word up to rotation, reversal and renaming; each band end attached to the inner or outer annulus boundary (4^n orientable surfaces); g = (n - b + 2)/2. The literal 'for any n != 4' is false at n = 1, 2 (source table GR_1 = GR_2 = {{0,1}}), a zero-credit wording defect; intended scope n >= 3, n != 4.
329080.mathematical_attempt_and_coverage: Proved: for n >= 5 the unique genus-range-{1,2} diagram is (123123)(44...nn); n = 3 unique R3; n = 4 exactly four; n = 1, 2 none. Proof: band deletion changes b by +-1 (heredity of min and max genus); bipartite interlacement graph gives genus 0; a shortest odd interlacement cycle is induced, and length >= 5 yields a 5-chord sub-diagram with no non-crossing chord, impossible by the finite 5-chord base lemma; so a triangle R3 exists; the base lemma applied to R3 plus any two other chords forces all extra chords into one arc as consecutive pairs. Existence via a new dart-model transfer lemma with state set {(1,T),(3,F),(3,T)} closed under appending isolated chords. Verification: dart model = ribbon model on 995,572 cases (n <= 5); GR_n matches source for n <= 6; deletion lemma on 4,948,896 cases; 5-chord base lemma by full enumeration (79 classes, 12 with max genus <= 2) and certificate (945 standard words: 492 satisfy P, 453 have a 1-face witness); transfer rules on 87,296 cases; hereditary classification to n = 9 confirms uniqueness (source computed n <= 7). Files: outputs/329080-proof.md, outputs/chord-*.json, scripts/chord*.py.
329080.remaining_gap: Lean formalization (Claude lane cannot compile): general cycle-count +-1 surgery lemma, transfer lemma induction, bipartite planar lemma, finite base check by decide, rotation bookkeeping. Semantic bridge: topological boundary count replaced by the standard dart/ribbon face count (the source itself computes via permutation cycles). Significance and routine-technique risk for root.

Since joining paths and adding glued triangles only add edges, this covers every H with at most 15 vertices.
